{"summary":"Re-review of the WP13 LINE template scope, limited to the supplied files. These repairs work: the template fingerprint is now inside the purpose-bound encrypted payload; the worker re-checks the vendor-scoped registration, the live state, and the stable event key against the current schedule or start time; old array payloads for order, commission and automation messages still pass `safePayload` and skip the webinar source check; and tenant scoping is kept. I found no schema, provider or router changes.

Two issues remain with the confirmation gate:
- **MAJOR (likely):** The confirmation is sent only when `lastMaterializedAt == null`. On a database that sorts NULLs last in ascending order, which is PostgreSQL's default, newly linked identities may never reach the 100-row materializer batch once a deployment has more than 100 identities.
- **MINOR:** The template's `updatedAt` is used as the cutoff for which bindings get a confirmation. Any edit to the template, such as a typo fix, permanently drops confirmations for bindings that the materializer hasn't processed yet.

Two lower-severity copy-preservation limits:
- **MINOR:** The length check at save time doesn't account for how text is packed into messages. A template can pass validation and then fail to render, which silently suppresses that trigger's notifications.
- **NIT:** A URL is only protected from splitting when it starts its own token, so a URL attached directly to Chinese text with no space can be split in an oversized token.

I made no claims about provider delivery, production data, test results or overall work-package readiness.","findings":[{"severity":"MAJOR","file":"src/lib/line-notification-materializer.ts","area":"identity selection orderBy (lastMaterializedAt asc) + confirmation gate `identity.lastMaterializedAt == null`","issue":"A registration confirmation is now sent only on the first time the materializer sees a binding (`lastMaterializedAt == null`). But identities are fetched with `orderBy: [{ lastMaterializedAt: "asc" }, { id: "asc" }]` and `take: 100`, across all tenants. On PostgreSQL, ascending order puts NULLs last by default. So once more than 100 non-revoked buyer_registration, buyer_order and promoter identities have a timestamp, those rows take every batch, and newly linked identities with a NULL timestamp are never selected.","evidence":"The materializer runs `findMany({ where: { revokedAt: null, subjectType: { in: [...] } }, orderBy: [{ lastMaterializedAt: "asc" }, { id: "asc" }], take: MATERIALIZE_LIMIT })` and then `if (isUpcoming(live, now) && identity.lastMaterializedAt == null)`. Each processed row is set to `lastMaterializedAt: now`, so it stays ahead of every NULL row. Nothing else creates confirmation rows.","impact":"Once a deployment has more than 100 active identities (any tenant), new bindings may never get a confirmation, and they also miss the reminder and live-started materialization. Any delay also makes the `updatedAt` cutoff drop more confirmations (see the next finding). If the schema instead gives `lastMaterializedAt` a default value, the `== null` gate never fires at all. Whether this happens depends on the database and schema; I can't confirm either from the supplied text.","recommended_fix":"Make the query put unobserved identities first, without a schema change. For example, use `orderBy: [{ lastMaterializedAt: { sort: "asc", nulls: "first" } }, { id: "asc" }]`, or run a separate first query for `lastMaterializedAt: null` before the rotation query. Also confirm that the schema column is nullable and has no default.","required_test":"Seed 150 identities that already have `lastMaterializedAt` set and one new verified buyer_registration identity with `lastMaterializedAt = null`, an upcoming live, and an active LINE confirmation template saved before it was linked. Run `materializeLineNotifications` once. Assert that the new identity is selected and a `registration_confirmed` delivery is queued.","confidence":0.55},{"severity":"MINOR","file":"src/lib/line-notification.ts","area":"enqueueLineNotification: `input.eventOccurredAt < template.updatedAt` → event_precedes_template","issue":"The cutoff deciding which bindings get a confirmation is the template's latest `updatedAt`, which changes on every save, not when the template was first saved or activated. If a merchant edits an active confirmation template after a student links but before the materializer first processes that identity, the confirmation is rejected. Because `lastMaterializedAt` is then set, it is never retried.","evidence":"The confirmation passes `eventOccurredAt: identity.linkedAt`. The check is `if (input.trigger === "registration_confirmed" && (!input.eventOccurredAt || input.eventOccurredAt < template.updatedAt)) return { status: "event_precedes_template" }`. After that, the materializer runs `lastMaterializedAt: now`. The UI only warns that edits stop already-queued notifications. It doesn't warn that edits drop confirmations for new bindings that haven't been queued yet.","impact":"Small edits such as typo fixes permanently drop confirmations for genuinely new bindings during the gap before the next materializer run. That gap can be long because of the 100-row global batch. Clock differences between the app instance that writes `linkedAt` and the one that writes `updatedAt` make it worse.","recommended_fix":"Gate on a stable boundary instead. Either rely on the first-observation flag (`lastMaterializedAt == null`) and drop the check for bindings observed after the deploy, or compare against a boundary that doesn't change on edits (such as when the template was first activated, if that is available without a schema change). Alternatively, document this behavior explicitly in the UI copy.","required_test":"Save an active LINE `registration_confirmed` template at T0. Link an identity at T1 > T0. Edit the template body at T2 > T1. Run the materializer at T3. Assert that the confirmation is queued with the T2 fingerprint, or, if dropping it is intended, that the UI copy states this.","confidence":0.6},{"severity":"MINOR","file":"src/lib/message-template.ts","area":"normalizeMessageTemplateDraft LINE expanded-length check vs splitLineText packing","issue":"The save-time check bounds the total expanded length at 25,000, which is five full 5,000-unit messages. But `splitLineText` packs whole tokens and opens a new chunk whenever the next token doesn't fit. Text under 25,000 units can therefore need more than five chunks. Examples are long Chinese paragraphs without spaces, around 2,600 to 5,000 units each, or repeated `{{live_url}}` expansions. In that case `splitLineText` returns null at send time.","evidence":"The save check is `maximum = subject + body + 2600 + Σ(limit - token)` with `maximum > 25_000` rejected. In `splitLineText`, `if (chunk.length + part.length > 5000) { chunks.push(chunk); chunk = "" }` and the result is null once there would be more than five chunks. In `enqueueLineNotification`, `if (!rendered) return { status: "template_disabled_or_invalid" }` with no fallback to the default message.","impact":"A merchant can save a LINE template that passes validation, and then every confirmation, reminder or live-started notification for that trigger is silently skipped, with no default fallback and no error shown to the merchant. The task accepts this as an edge-case limitation, but it is concrete and invisible.","recommended_fix":"At save time, render the template with maximum-length placeholder values and run `splitLineText` on the result. Reject the template if it returns null. Optionally record or surface the `template_disabled_or_invalid` outcome so the merchant can see it.","required_test":"Use a body made of six paragraphs of 3,000 CJK characters each, separated by newlines (total under 25,000). Assert that `normalizeMessageTemplateDraft` and `buildLineWebinarMessages` agree: either the save is rejected or the template renders into at most five messages.","confidence":0.7},{"severity":"NIT","file":"src/lib/line-webinar-template.ts","area":"splitLineText token regex / oversized-token URL guard","issue":"A URL is only protected from splitting when it starts its own token. A URL attached to preceding text with no space, which is common in Chinese copy like `連結：{{live_url}}` and matches the generated `進場連結：${live_url}` line, is matched as part of a generic `\S+` token. If that token is longer than 5,000 units, the `/^https?:\/\//` guard doesn't apply, and the token is split at grapheme boundaries, possibly in the middle of the URL.","evidence":"The token regex is `/https?:\/\/\S+|\S+|\s+/gu`. At the position of `進`, the `\S+` alternative consumes the whole run including the URL. The guard is `if (/^https?:\/\//u.test(token)) return null;` and only checks the start of the token.","impact":"In the oversized-token edge case, a merchant URL can be split across two LINE messages and stop being clickable. That contradicts the claim that URLs are preserved in this situation. Tokens of 5,000 units or fewer are unaffected.","recommended_fix":"Tokenize URLs anywhere in the text, for example `/https?:\/\/[^\s]+|[^\s]+?(?=https?:\/\/)|\S+|\s+/gu`. Alternatively, before splitting at graphemes, check whether the oversized token contains `https?://` and either split before the URL or return null.","required_test":"Use a body with 5,200 CJK characters directly followed by `{{live_url}}` and no whitespace. Assert that the URL appears intact in exactly one output message, or that the render is rejected.","confidence":0.75}]}
